# Structural collection extraction reference

The name population comes from the closed ASCII grammar and the Windows device namespace:
CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 through COM9 and LPT1 through LPT9. Every letter-case permutation
and empty, single, uppercase or compound extension is exercised at shared index admission.
Superscript 1/2/3 device spellings and the special console names are included; the latter
also violate the closed ASCII alphabet. Ordinary positive controls use unambiguous names,
without imposing a separate acceptance policy for COM0 or LPT0.
The reference is [Microsoft's file naming rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file).
No network fetch of that reference is part of the gate. Independent ordinary-name controls
prevent a blanket rejection from satisfying the grammar. Excluded ASCII characters, Unicode,
leading dots and a segment exceeding the Windows component length are exercised separately.

An index and archive are authored by the destination fixture, with standard-library digests.
Representative reserved names also reach every public/legacy entrance and archive extraction.
A cache constructed solely from authored project bytes has no completion marker by construction;
it must be fetched again and receive all archive members. Cache layout is the documented
collection layout, not a numerical or scientific implementation oracle.

A second cache witness changes the final digit of the declared SHA-256 while retaining
its cache-name prefix and the actual source bytes. A marker bound to the old full digest
must not admit that cache: refetch must reach the independent digest mismatch. The gate
does not depend on the completion marker's filename or serialization.

The Linux-only preload fixture injects a one-shot write, flush or close refusal at a file named
`project.edi` below the controlled operation root. It observes standard GNU filebuf operations
and POSIX/stdio operations, including directory-relative calls, not downloader function names.
Independent C++, stdio and POSIX writers prove all requested fault channels before the
subject runs. No downloader code is linked. An
independent writer first proves each requested failure channel; the actual extraction must
then reach the same channel. No reached channel means no fault qualification. Failure must
be reported, publish nothing and remove private staging. No disk limits or system files change.

Build explicitly under the shared build lock with `build.py DESTINATION`; its sole CMake build
uses `-j 4`. Set `EDI_FILE_FAILURE_FIXTURE_DIR` for the scoped run. Its source receipt must
match; tests do not auto-build. This proves Linux GNU stream faults only, not other C++ ABIs.

Before this extension, the boundary observer rejected all transient parent writes. It now
permits a fresh parent staging directory only when its lifecycle ends in removal or a move;
existing outside objects and final outside state remain protected. The structural witness
separately requires caller-owned staging with no group or other permission bits in the
requested output folder's parent. Kernel directory events distinguish a single publication
rename from a copied tree, even when their final bytes match, and reject transient partial
publication on failure. An independent standard-library publisher passes that same validator
with successful I/O and each injected refusal; it supplies no production expected values.

Both local and recorded HTTPS replies exercise unmarked-cache refetch and full-digest
completion admission. The recorded trace must contain the authored archive request and no
real network attempt. Explicit directory/file conflict exercises failed directory creation.
These behavioral checks do not prove that only one core implementation exists or that the
completion marker is physically written last; those remain source-review obligations.
